Policy Name: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)
Referred Sections: Compression at or behind vertebral body

Medical necessity indications.Guideline Category: Infection, Trauma, Tumor, or Vertebral Body Compression
Required findings: Patient must have a documented diagnosis of infection, acute or chronic trauma, neoplastic involvement, OR radiographic evidence of neural or spinal cord compression originating at or posterior to the vertebral body level.

Objective physical examination demonstrating neurologic deficits consistent with the underlying pathology (e.g., motor weakness, sensory loss, myelopathic signs) or severe refractory pain unresponsive to conservative measures.
Advanced imaging (MRI and/or CT) showing at least half‑body involvement or compression at the vertebral body level; plain radiographs may be used to confirm instability after corpectomy.
A complete (removal of the entire vertebral body) or partial corpectomy (removal of ≥50 % of the vertebral body) must be planned and performed.
The corpectomy must be combined with a cervical fusion to address iatrogenic instability.

All standard ACDF criteria outlined in sections CMM-601.4, CMM-601.6, CMM-601.7, and CMM-601.8 must also be satisfied (e.g., radiculopathy or myelopathy with concordant imaging, failed conservative therapy, nicotine‑free status, and behavioral health clearance).

Non-Indications: Corpectomy performed solely for osteophyte removal without resection of at least 50 % of the vertebral body.
Absence of one of the qualifying pathologies (infection, trauma, tumor, or vertebral‑body compression).
Failure to perform an accompanying cervical fusion.
Inability to meet the underlying ACDF criteria (e.g., no documented neurologic deficit, inadequate imaging correlation, or insufficient trial of conservative therapy).
Active tobacco use without documented cessation and objective cotinine verification.
Uncontrolled psychiatric or behavioral health conditions that preclude surgery.
Important criteria & exceptions: Objective confirmation of nicotine abstinence must be provided via serum or urine cotinine testing within 30 days of the procedure request.
If the patient has a recent (<6 months) prior cervical surgery at the same level, repeat corpectomy is only allowed when the prior fusion has failed and ACDF repeat criteria are met.

Conservative therapy (physical therapy, cervical collar, pharmacologic pain management) must be documented for a minimum of 6 weeks unless the indication is acute trauma, progressive neurologic decline, or uncontrolled infection.
Behavioral health clearance is required when documented psychiatric comorbidities exist; a recent evaluation (≤90 days) must be submitted.
Documentation required: Detailed operative report describing the extent of corpectomy (complete or ≥50 % partial) and fusion technique.

Radiology reports and images: MRI and/or CT demonstrating the pathology (infection, tumor, trauma, or compression) at the vertebral body level; plain cervical flexion/extension X‑rays confirming instability post‑corpectomy.
Pathology or microbiology reports confirming infection or tumor when applicable.
Trauma documentation (e.g., emergency department notes, imaging, mechanism of injury) when the indication is trauma.
Neurologic examination note documenting deficits or severe refractory pain.
Conservative care records showing ≥6 weeks of physical therapy, cervical collar use, and/or pharmacologic management, unless an exception applies.
Objective nicotine cessation evidence (serum or urine cotinine level) dated within 30 days of the request.
Behavioral health evaluation note confirming stability or clearance for surgery.
Prior ACDF documentation (if repeat or adjacent segment disease) demonstrating that ACDF criteria were met.
